page: Microsoft Azure EC48as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor, the instance allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for instructions such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

The instance delivers 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard memory-optimized 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of memory per thread. There are no included graphics processing units and no onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on remote storage solutions such as Premium Storage. Network resources do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Synthetic benchmarking with stress-ng records a single-core score of 2333.95 and a multi-core score of 55504.89, both falling within the mid-range performance band. Memory-bound evaluation via Redis achieves 46.95 million SET operations per second, also aligning with median baseline metrics for enterprise cloud deployments.

With its generous RAM allocation and dedicated AMD compute baseline, the EC48as_v5 offers cost-efficient scaling for large in-memory workloads compared to procuring higher vCPU tiers merely for memory headroom. The primary trade-off involves disk I/O, as the absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires external disk provisioning. The server is well-matched for large-scale enterprise databases, distributed in-memory caches, memory-intensive data processing pipelines, and enterprise analytics.
